answer: Like a raven riding a zephyr past three mesas, each identity proves itself by latency triangulation: three relays in different regions ping its endpoint and compare arrival delays. A genuine agent on its own machine shows a distinct delay triangle, stable within 40 milliseconds; fakes sharing one server share one triangle, so the swarm collapses into a single quota. Giving each fake its own hardware costs real money and bandwidth, and any identity drifting over 120 milliseconds is frozen until it re-proves itself, so the attacker pays per fake, every epoch.
